title: Decoding systemic vascular health and hypertensive disorders in pregnancy through retinal imaging and Visionary AI - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Visionary AI converts ultrawidefield maternal retinal images into graph, geometric and topological vascular features to predict hypertensive disorders of pregnancy months before diagnosis, reaching AUC 0.91 in a 1,267-pregnancy Columbia cohort and transferring without retraining to an independent 79-pregnancy NYU cohort at AUC 0.81 versus 0.73 for the Fetal Medicine Foundation calculator. Both RETFound and an Inception-ResNet-v2 CNN performed near chance externally, which the authors attribute to dimensionality reduction being advantageous in low-event clinical cohorts.

themes.theme: The first-trimester screening gap and its economics

insights.claim: Hypertensive disorders affect 2-15% of pregnancies and are the second leading cause of maternal mortality worldwide, yet they are typically diagnosed only after 20 weeks when hypertension, proteinuria or organ dysfunction become clinically apparent.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A large, universal obstetric population is currently screened by a method that fires too late to act on, which is the structural opening any first-trimester test is selling into.
insights.quote: HDPs are typically diagnosed after 20 weeks of gestation, when symptoms such as hypertension, proteinuria or organ dysfunction become clinically apparent.
insights.locator: Despite their burden

insights.claim: The value of early prediction is anchored to a specific intervention window: randomized trials show low-dose aspirin started before 16 weeks can cut the risk of preterm delivery with preeclampsia by up to 62%, but only if risk is identified early and accurately.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Prediction is only monetizable inside a sub-16-week window with an existing cheap drug, which sets both the deadline and the reimbursement logic for any screening product.
insights.quote: randomized trials show that early initiation of low-dose aspirin (before 16 weeks) can reduce the risk of preterm delivery with preeclampsia by up to 62%22,23 but this requires early, accurate risk identification.
insights.locator: From a health systems perspective

insights.claim: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were estimated at 2.18 billion USD in annual US healthcare costs as of 2012, largely driven by preterm birth complications, with incidence rising since and affected pregnancies ending roughly three weeks earlier than normotensive ones.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Quantifies the payer-side prize and the mechanism (gestational age at delivery) through which a screening-plus-aspirin pathway would show savings.
insights.quote: HDPs accounted for an estimated 2.18 billion USD in US healthcare costs per year (estimated in 2012), largely driven by preterm birth complications
insights.locator: From a health systems perspective

insights.claim: Existing tools each fail at a different point: clinical risk factors lack individual-level accuracy, the best-validated biomarker (sFlt-1/PlGF) is mainly useful later in pregnancy for suspected cases, and first-trimester protocols combining biomarkers or ultrasound are expensive, logistically complex and inconsistently implemented.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The competitive gap is not accuracy alone but accuracy achievable inside routine low-cost workflows, which favors imaging-based tests over assay panels.
insights.quote: First-trimester screening tools, such as the Fetal Medicine Foundation (FMF) risk calculator27, combine clinical variables with biomarkers or ultrasound but these protocols are expensive, logistically complex and inconsistently implemented
insights.locator: Current diagnostic criteria for preeclampsia rely on late-onset symptoms

insights.claim: In routine practice, prevention-oriented risk stratification collapses into coarse aspirin-eligibility screening that both misses emerging vascular dysfunction and labels broad groups as high risk; at NYU, ACOG-based eligibility caught 62% of cases at a 47% false positive rate and a prevalence-adjusted PPV of 0.1.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The real-world incumbent is not a model but a checklist with near-coin-flip specificity, a far weaker benchmark than published calculators suggest.
insights.quote: In the NYU cohort, aspirin eligibility identified preeclampsia cases with a TPR of 0.62 but at a substantially higher FPR of 0.47 and lower prevalence-adjusted PPV of 0.1.
insights.locator: We also compared Visionary AI to the clinical risk-stratification approach used at NYU

insights.claim: The central thesis is that the maternal retina is a minimally invasive readout of systemic vascular health, with early-pregnancy retinal structure carrying quantifiable microvascular signatures of systemic dysfunction that precede clinical preeclampsia diagnosis.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If the retina proxies systemic endothelial state, the same imaging asset could be repurposed across cardiovascular and metabolic risk prediction, not just obstetrics.
insights.quote: Recurrent features involving retinal vascular topology, geometry, network complexity and hierarchical organization position the maternal retina as a minimally invasive biosensor of systemic vascular health

insights.claim: The biological case rests on prior observations of retinal change in established preeclampsia, including arteriolar narrowing, reduced capillary density in superficial and deep plexuses, and the team's own postpartum finding of significantly increased inferotemporal retinal artery tortuosity in 31 severe preeclampsia cases versus 35 normotensive controls.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Grounds the model in a pre-existing physiological literature, which matters for regulatory and clinical acceptance in a field skeptical of opaque imaging classifiers.
insights.quote: A prior postpartum study from our team (31 severe preeclampsia cases and 35 normotensive controls) demonstrated significantly increased median tortuosity in the inferotemporal retinal artery among individuals with preeclampsia
insights.locator: Increasing evidence suggests a link between placental vascular changes

insights.claim: Preeclampsia is framed as plural rather than singular: recent systems biology work suggests multiple distinct biological pathways, with early-onset disease more associated with placental dysfunction and late-onset disease more with maternal processes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A single risk score may be modeling a composite of mechanistically different diseases, which bounds how far any one model can generalize across subtypes.
insights.quote: recent systems biology studies suggest that preeclampsia is not a single disease entity but may reflect multiple distinct biological pathways, with EOPE more frequently associated with placental dysfunction and LOPE more often associated

insights.claim: Model features are interpreted as two converging pathological processes, capillary rarefaction (loss of small vessels, reduced density, impaired branching) and arteriolar wall thickening that narrows lumens and raises resistance, which jointly reduce network redundancy and raise ischemic susceptibility.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Gives the score a mechanistic story clinicians can act on, which is the difference between a research classifier and something that changes surveillance decisions.
insights.quote: Visionary AI captures early signs of vascular simplification, a hallmark of preeclampsia, consistent with two complementary pathological processes: capillary network rarefaction

themes.theme: Interpretable vascular features beat image-level deep learning

insights.claim: Both deep-learning baselines collapsed on external data: RETFound, a retinal foundation model fine-tuned with its developers' own scripts, and a transfer-learned Inception-ResNet-v2 performed near chance in the NYU cohort, while the feature-based Visionary AI held AUC 0.81.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: In rare-outcome clinical cohorts, foundation-model fine-tuning can lose outright to engineered low-dimensional features, which cuts against the default assumption that pretrained imaging models dominate.
insights.quote: Under these training and evaluation configurations, both image-level baselines performed near chance in the NYU cohort (Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7), whereas Visionary AI maintained strong predictive performance in external validation.
insights.locator: For external evaluation, the CU-trained RETFound

insights.claim: The authors explicitly decline the strong claim their own result invites, stating the comparison does not establish general superiority over deep learning and that end-to-end models may simply need far more outcome events than prospective pregnancy cohorts provide.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Positions the advantage as event-count-contingent rather than architectural, implying the moat narrows as prospective cohorts scale.
insights.quote: The results therefore do not establish that Visionary AI is generally superior to deep learning.
insights.locator: We interpret these findings cautiously

insights.claim: The design principle is dimensionality reduction with biological structure preserved: images become vessel segmentation maps and then graph, geometric, nesting-tree and complexity features, rather than opaque embeddings, which the authors argue suits limited-event cohorts.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A reusable recipe for medical AI where positives are scarce: encode domain structure to shrink the hypothesis space instead of scaling the model.

insights.claim: Prior retinal-AI attempts for preeclampsia were limited in ways this work targets: the PROMPT model leaned on clinical variables like mean arterial pressure and reached only AUC 0.74 image-only at a single site, another used an uninterpretable CNN, and both were run in homogeneous East Asian populations.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Sets the prior art bar at ~0.74 single-site and identifies population homogeneity as the standing weakness, which is what external multi-ethnic validation is meant to clear.
insights.quote: The PROMPT model (preeclampsia risk factor + ophthalmic data + mean arterial pressure prediction test)41 relied heavily on clinical variables (for example, mean arterial pressure) and achieved modest image-only performance using
insights.locator: Initial efforts to apply AI to HDP prediction using retinal imaging

themes.theme: Optimizing for stability instead of peak performance

insights.claim: The authors deliberately built two models with different objectives, a performance-optimized one for internal Columbia performance and a stability-optimized one selected on low average-precision variability and high minimum AUC across five nonoverlapping control settings, and used the stability model for external validation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Treating cross-control-set stability as the selection criterion is a transferable antidote to the leaderboard overfitting that sinks most clinical ML at deployment.
insights.quote: a stability-optimized CU model was designed to prioritize reproducibility across nonoverlapping population-wide control groups rather than maximize within-site performance
insights.locator: Therefore, we evaluated Visionary AI across three increasingly stringent settings

insights.claim: Stability selection cut model complexity by an order of magnitude, contracting an initial search space of 96 candidate base learners spanning 32 retinal vascular feature sets and three model classes down to eight nonredundant base learners per fold.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Radical pruning preserved external signal, evidence that most of the ensemble was control-set-specific noise rather than usable predictive capacity.
insights.quote: The initial search space included 96 candidate base learners, representing 32 retinal vascular feature sets across three model classes.
insights.locator: This stability-based procedure substantially reduced model complexity

insights.claim: Performance was reported across three deliberately escalating difficulty tiers, with the high-contrast curated-healthy-control comparison reaching AUC 0.94 and AP 0.92 but explicitly disclaimed as proof of signal rather than clinical performance because the contrast was intentionally enriched.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A template for honest staged reporting, and a warning that headline AUCs from curated-control studies in this space are not comparable to population-wide numbers.
insights.quote: We interpret this analysis as an initial proof of signal rather than as the primary estimate of clinical performance, as the comparison was intentionally enriched for phenotypic contrast.
insights.locator: Visionary AI distinguished participants who later developed preeclampsia

insights.claim: Prevalence sensitivity is handled head-on: the NYU cohort's observed 17.7% preeclampsia prevalence far exceeded the institutional ~8% average, so adjusted metrics show the stringent operating point's PPV falling from 0.86 observed to 0.68 adjusted and the lenient point from 0.56 to 0.31.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Shows how much reported precision in small validation cohorts is prevalence artifact, a correction most competing screening claims omit.
insights.quote: Under this prevalence-adjusted setting, the stringent operating point corresponded to an estimated PPV of 0.68 and NPV 0.95, whereas the less stringent operating point corresponded to an estimated PPV of 0.31 and NPV of 0.97
insights.locator: Because the observed preeclampsia prevalence in the NYU validation cohort was higher

themes.theme: Clinical positioning versus existing risk tools

insights.claim: Adding the Fetal Medicine Foundation calculator's probabilities to Visionary AI did not materially improve performance in either cohort (CU AUC 0.90 versus 0.91 alone; aspirin subgroup 0.78 combined versus 0.95 alone), suggesting retinal features already subsume the clinical risk signal.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If an imaging-only test absorbs the information in clinical risk factors, the multimodal-panel approach that first-trimester screening vendors sell loses its rationale.
insights.quote: Combining Visionary AI predictions with FMF probabilities did not materially improve performance over Visionary AI alone.
insights.locator: a, ROC and PR curves for the performance-optimized Visionary AI model

insights.claim: The model retained strong performance precisely where risk stratification is hardest, reaching AUC 0.95 and AP 0.85 within the 33 NYU participants already recommended aspirin, versus FMF AUC 0.76, indicating information orthogonal to the criteria that flagged those women.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Supports a second-line triage business model inside an already-identified high-risk pool, which is an easier adoption path than replacing universal screening.
insights.quote: In this aspirin-recommended subgroup, Visionary AI maintained strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.95 and an AP of 0.85, compared to the FMF AUC of 0.76 and AP of 0.65
insights.locator: As an additional sensitivity analysis

insights.claim: Deployment economics are framed as the differentiator rather than accuracy: retinal fundus imaging needs no laboratory infrastructure, takes under two minutes, can be operated by nonspecialists, and the automated pipeline removes manual image grading and its subjectivity.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Points the addressable market at low-resource obstetric care where biomarker panels and ultrasound-based protocols cannot run at all.
insights.quote: Retinal fundus imaging requires no laboratory infrastructure, takes less than 2 min to perform and can be operated by nonspecialists.
insights.locator: Visionary AI offers a fast, noninvasive and cost-effective screening strategy

insights.claim: The authors leave the deployment model explicitly unresolved, listing standalone screening, a multimodal model with clinical and biomarker approaches, or a second-line test for already high-risk individuals as alternatives requiring further prospective study.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Calibration, thresholds and workflow integration are still open, which is where the regulatory and reimbursement risk in this asset actually sits.
insights.quote: Additional prospective studies will be needed to determine whether Visionary AI is best deployed as a standalone screening tool, as part of a multimodal model with established clinical and biomarker-based approaches or as a second-line
insights.locator: Visionary AI may provide value as a retinal microvascular adjunct

themes.theme: Disease-specific vascular signatures and generalization limits

insights.claim: The framework extended beyond preeclampsia to gestational hypertension (performance-optimized AUC 0.91, AP 0.83 over 49 cases) and chronic hypertension (AUC 0.90, AP 0.79 over 61 cases), though stability-optimized versions dropped to AUC 0.80/0.78 and the NYU gestational hypertension test on seven cases gave only AUC 0.67.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Breadth across hypertensive phenotypes widens the clinical claim, but the gap between internal and external numbers shows generalization, not signal, is the binding constraint.
insights.quote: The performance-optimized model achieved an AUC of 0.91 ± 0.05 and an AP of 0.83 ± 0.07 for GHTN (n = 1,132, including 49 GHTN cases) and an AUC of 0.90 ± 0.06 and an AP of 0.79 ± 0.12 for CHTN
insights.locator: To this end, we used both the performance and stability-optimized model architectures

insights.claim: Different hypertensive disorders produced distinguishable vascular geometries: gestational and chronic hypertension showed localized simplification of hierarchical organization, while preeclampsia showed global sparsity and disorganization with increased tortuosity and fewer loops, and the two hypertension models weighted topological data analysis features differently (flooding versus outward).
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If signatures are disease-specific rather than a generic hypertension readout, the same image could support differential diagnosis, not just a single risk score.
insights.quote: Taken together, these differences indicate a simplification of hierarchical vascular organization in GHTN and CHTN, pointing to localized changes, whereas preeclampsia had greater sparsity and disorganization on a global level
insights.locator: Furthermore, while the GHTN model gives greater importance to topological data analysis

insights.claim: Cohort differences were treated as a feature of the validation design, with the authors arguing that divergence in race and ethnicity distribution, maternal age, IVF prevalence, clinical workflow and Optos imaging device (Primary versus California) makes NYU a genuine external test rather than a near-replication.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Device and workflow heterogeneity is the usual failure mode for imaging AI, so building it into the validation rather than controlling it out is a stronger evidentiary claim.
insights.quote: Together, these demographic, clinical, workflow and imaging-device differences support the use of NYU as a meaningful external validation cohort rather than a near replication of the CU development cohort.
insights.locator: The NYU cohort differed from the CU cohort in several clinically relevant respects

insights.claim: The evidence base remains thin in absolute terms: only 54 Columbia and 13 NYU preeclampsia cases entered retinal analyses, subtype analyses such as early-onset preeclampsia (one NYU case) were post hoc stratifications of a single overall model, and all data come from two US academic medical centers.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Event counts this small mean confidence intervals, calibration and thresholds are unsettled, so claims of clinical readiness should be discounted pending multisite validation.
insights.quote: Although our prospective CU development cohort was large for imaging-based pregnancy research, the absolute number of preeclampsia cases was modest because of low baseline prevalence.
insights.locator: Several limitations warrant consideration

insights.claim: A bespoke segmentation model underpins the whole pipeline: an RV-GAN-inspired U-Net generator was pretrained on public 45-degree color fundus datasets then fine-tuned on just 20 hand-annotated ultrawidefield images from the study cohort, with probability maps binarized at 0.3 to preserve fine vessels.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The platform depends on a hand-annotated 20-image fine-tune and a hard threshold choice, a fragile upstream link that any replication or device transfer would stress first.
insights.quote: It was then fine-tuned on a curated set of 20 ultrawidefield retinal images from the study cohort with corresponding hand-annotated vessel maps.
insights.locator: AI-based vessel segmentation and VSI generation
